title: Behavioral Forgetting Is Not Privacy in Machine Unlearning
abstract: arXiv:2610.21799v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine unlearning aims to remove targeted information from large language models, but existing evaluations often measure forgetting only on a designated benchmark distribution. We argue that such behavioral forgetting is an insufficient standard for privacy-oriented unlearning, and that evaluation should instead test whether forgetting persists across the access paths through which the same information may be recovered. We demonstrate this with a controlled case study of cross-lingual querying: across multiple multilingual model families, forgetting varies substantially when semantically equivalent information is queried in different languages and scripts. A single access path is therefore enough to expose a real gap between behavioral forgetting and information inaccessibility, motivating broader evaluation of access-path generalization and adversarial recoverability alongside in-distribution forgetting.

translated_title: 机器遗忘中的行为性遗忘并不等于隐私保护
translated_abstract: 机器遗忘旨在从大语言模型中移除目标信息，但现有评估通常仅在指定的基准分布上衡量遗忘效果。我们认为，对于面向隐私的遗忘而言，这种行为性遗忘是一个不充分的标准，评估应当转而检验遗忘是否能在可能恢复相同信息的各类访问路径上持续存在。我们通过一个跨语言查询的受控案例研究证明了这一点：在多个多语言模型家族中，当用不同语言和文字查询语义等价的信息时，遗忘效果差异显著。因此，仅凭单一访问路径就足以暴露行为性遗忘与信息不可访问性之间的真实差距，这促使我们在分布内遗忘之外，对访问路径的泛化能力和对抗性可恢复性进行更广泛的评估。
tldr: 本文指出机器遗忘中的行为性遗忘不等于隐私保护，因为通过跨语言查询等不同访问路径仍可恢复被“遗忘”的信息，因此遗忘评估应检验信息在各类访问路径上的不可访问性与对抗性可恢复性。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that behavioral forgetting in machine unlearning is not equivalent to privacy, since forgotten information can still be recovered through alternative access paths such as cross-lingual queries, and evaluation should therefore test information inaccessibility and adversarial recoverability across access paths.
